raw: CHAPTER X. The Substance of the Shadow
en: [Chapter 10]

raw: “I, Alexandre Manette, unfortunate physician, native of Beauvais, and afterwards resident in Paris, write this melancholy paper in my doleful cell in the Bastille, during the last month of the year, 1767.
en: The Substance of the Shadow “I, Alexandre Manette, an unfortunate doctor from Beauvais who later lived in Paris, write this sad paper in my dark cell in the Bastille during the last month of the year 1767.

raw: I write it at stolen intervals, under every difficulty.
en: I write it in secret moments, facing every difficulty.

raw: I design to secrete it in the wall of the chimney, where I have slowly and laboriously made a place of concealment for it.
en: I plan to hide it in the chimney wall, where I have slowly and carefully made a hiding place for it.

raw: Some pitying hand may find it there, when I and my sorrows are dust.
en: Some kind hand may find it there when I and my sorrows are nothing but dust.

raw: “These words are formed by the rusty iron point with which I write with difficulty in scrapings of soot and charcoal from the chimney, mixed with blood, in the last month of the tenth year of my captivity.
en: “These words are written with a rusty iron point, which I use with great difficulty, using soot and charcoal scraped from the chimney and mixed with my own blood. It is now the last month of the tenth year of my imprisonment.

raw: Hope has quite departed from my breast.
en: Hope has completely left my heart.

raw: I know from terrible warnings I have noted in myself that my reason will not long remain unimpaired, but I solemnly declare that I am at this time in the possession of my right mind--that my memory is exact and circumstantial--and that I write the truth as I shall answer for these my last recorded words, whether they be ever read by men or not, at the Eternal Judgment-seat.
en: I know from terrible warning signs in myself that my mind will not stay clear for much longer. However, I solemnly declare that right now I am in my right mind, that my memory is exact and detailed, and that I write the truth as I will have to answer for these last recorded words at God's final judgment, whether they are ever read by men or not.

raw: “One cloudy moonlight night, in the third week of December (I think the twenty-second of the month) in the year 1757, I was walking on a retired part of the quay by the Seine for the refreshment of the frosty air, at an hour’s distance from my place of residence in the Street of the School of Medicine, when a carriage came along behind me, driven very fast.
en: “One cloudy, moonlit night in the third week of December, I think it was the twenty-second, in the year 1757, I was walking on a quiet part of the path along the Seine River to get some fresh, frosty air. I was about an hour's walk from my home on the Street of the School of Medicine when a carriage came up behind me, driving very fast.

raw: As I stood aside to let that carriage pass, apprehensive that it might otherwise run me down, a head was put out at the window, and a voice called to the driver to stop.
en: I stepped aside to let the carriage pass, worried that it might run me over, when a head popped out of the window and a voice called for the driver to stop.

raw: “The carriage stopped as soon as the driver could rein in his horses, and the same voice called to me by my name.
en: “The carriage stopped as soon as the driver could pull back his horses, and the same voice called out my name.

raw: I answered.
en: I answered.

raw: The carriage was then so far in advance of me that two gentlemen had time to open the door and alight before I came up with it.
en: The carriage was so far ahead of me that two gentlemen had time to open the door and step down before I reached it.

raw: “I observed that they were both wrapped in cloaks, and appeared to conceal themselves.
en: “I noticed that they were both wrapped in cloaks and seemed to be hiding their identities.

raw: As they stood side by side near the carriage door, I also observed that they both looked of about my own age, or rather younger, and that they were greatly alike, in stature, manner, voice, and (as far as I could see) face too.
en: As they stood side by side near the carriage door, I also noticed that they both looked to be about my age, or perhaps younger, and they were extremely similar in height, behavior, voice, and, from what I could see, face as well.

raw: “‘You are Doctor Manette?’ said one.
en: “‘Are you Doctor Manette?’ one asked.

raw: “I am.”
en: “I am.”

raw: “‘Doctor Manette, formerly of Beauvais,’ said the other; ‘the young physician, originally an expert surgeon, who within the last year or two has made a rising reputation in Paris?’
en: “‘Doctor Manette, formerly of Beauvais,’ said the other, ‘the young doctor, originally a skilled surgeon, who has made a growing reputation in Paris over the last year or two?’

raw: “‘Gentlemen,’ I returned, ‘I am that Doctor Manette of whom you speak so graciously.’
en: “‘Gentlemen,’ I replied, ‘I am indeed the Doctor Manette you speak of so kindly.’

raw: “‘We have been to your residence,’ said the first, ‘and not being so fortunate as to find you there, and being informed that you were probably walking in this direction, we followed, in the hope of overtaking you.
en: “‘We went to your home,’ said the first man, ‘but we were not lucky enough to find you. When we were told you were probably walking in this direction, we followed you, hoping to catch up.

raw: Will you please to enter the carriage?’
en: Please get into the carriage.’

raw: “The manner of both was imperious, and they both moved, as these words were spoken, so as to place me between themselves and the carriage door.
en: “The manner of both men was very commanding, and as they spoke, they moved to trap me between them and the carriage door.

raw: They were armed.
en: They were armed.

raw: I was not.
en: I was not.

raw: “‘Gentlemen,’ said I, ‘pardon me; but I usually inquire who does me the honour to seek my assistance, and what is the nature of the case to which I am summoned.’
en: “‘Gentlemen,’ I said, ‘excuse me, but I usually ask who is asking for my help, and what kind of medical case I am being called to see.’

raw: “The reply to this was made by him who had spoken second. ‘Doctor, your clients are people of condition.
en: “The second man replied to this. ‘Doctor, your patients are people of high social standing.

raw: As to the nature of the case, our confidence in your skill assures us that you will ascertain it for yourself better than we can describe it.
en: As for the nature of the illness, we are so confident in your skill that we know you will figure it out for yourself better than we could describe it.

raw: Enough.
en: That is enough.

raw: Will you please to enter the carriage?’
en: Please get into the carriage.’

raw: “I could do nothing but comply, and I entered it in silence.
en: “I had no choice but to obey, and I got in silently.

raw: They both entered after me--the last springing in, after putting up the steps.
en: They both followed me, the last one jumping in after folding up the carriage steps.

raw: The carriage turned about, and drove on at its former speed.
en: The carriage turned around and drove off at the same high speed as before.

raw: “I repeat this conversation exactly as it occurred.
en: “I repeat this conversation exactly as it happened.

raw: I have no doubt that it is, word for word, the same.
en: I have no doubt it is word-for-word correct.

raw: I describe everything exactly as it took place, constraining my mind not to wander from the task.
en: I describe everything exactly as it occurred, forcing my mind not to wander from the task.

raw: Where I make the broken marks that follow here, I leave off for the time, and put my paper in its hiding-place. *****
en: Wherever I make the star marks that follow, it means I stopped writing for a while and put my paper back in its hiding place.

raw: “The carriage left the streets behind, passed the North Barrier, and emerged upon the country road.
en: “The carriage left the city streets, passed through the North Gate, and went onto a country road.

raw: At two-thirds of a league from the Barrier--I did not estimate the distance at that time, but afterwards when I traversed it--it struck out of the main avenue, and presently stopped at a solitary house, We all three alighted, and walked, by a damp soft footpath in a garden where a neglected fountain had overflowed, to the door of the house.
en: About two miles from the gate, I did not measure the distance then, but did so later when I traveled it again, the carriage turned off the main road and soon stopped at a lonely house. The three of us got out and walked down a damp, soft garden path, past a neglected, overflowing fountain, to the door.

raw: It was not opened immediately, in answer to the ringing of the bell, and one of my two conductors struck the man who opened it, with his heavy riding glove, across the face.
en: It was not opened right away when we rang the bell, so one of my guides struck the servant who finally opened it across the face with his heavy riding glove.

raw: “There was nothing in this action to attract my particular attention, for I had seen common people struck more commonly than dogs.
en: “There was nothing unusual in this to catch my attention, for I had seen common people beaten more often than dogs.

raw: But, the other of the two, being angry likewise, struck the man in like manner with his arm; the look and bearing of the brothers were then so exactly alike, that I then first perceived them to be twin brothers.
en: But the other gentleman, who was also angry, struck the servant in the same way with his arm. The looks and actions of the two men were so identical that I realized for the first time they were twin brothers.

raw: “From the time of our alighting at the outer gate (which we found locked, and which one of the brothers had opened to admit us, and had relocked), I had heard cries proceeding from an upper chamber.
en: “From the moment we got out at the outer gate, which we found locked, and which one of the brothers unlocked to let us in and then locked again, I had heard screams coming from an upstairs room.

raw: I was conducted to this chamber straight, the cries growing louder as we ascended the stairs, and I found a patient in a high fever of the brain, lying on a bed.
en: I was taken straight to this room, the screams growing louder as we climbed the stairs, and I found a patient with a severe brain fever lying on a bed.

raw: “The patient was a woman of great beauty, and young; assuredly not much past twenty.
en: “The patient was a very beautiful young woman, certainly not much over twenty.

raw: Her hair was torn and ragged, and her arms were bound to her sides with sashes and handkerchiefs.
en: Her hair was torn and messy, and her arms were tied to her sides with sashes and handkerchiefs.

raw: I noticed that these bonds were all portions of a gentleman’s dress.
en: I noticed that these ties were all parts of a gentleman's clothing.

raw: On one of them, which was a fringed scarf for a dress of ceremony, I saw the armorial bearings of a Noble, and the letter E.
en: On one of them, which was a fringed scarf used for formal wear, I saw the coat of arms of a nobleman and the letter E.

raw: “I saw this, within the first minute of my contemplation of the patient; for, in her restless strivings she had turned over on her face on the edge of the bed, had drawn the end of the scarf into her mouth, and was in danger of suffocation.
en: “I saw this during my very first minute of examining the patient. In her restless struggling, she had turned over onto her face at the edge of the bed, drawing the end of the scarf into her mouth, and was in danger of choking.

raw: My first act was to put out my hand to relieve her breathing; and in moving the scarf aside, the embroidery in the corner caught my sight.
en: My first act was to reach out and help her breathe, and as I moved the scarf away, I saw the embroidered coat of arms in the corner.

raw: “I turned her gently over, placed my hands upon her breast to calm her and keep her down, and looked into her face.
en: “I turned her over gently, placed my hands on her chest to calm her and keep her still, and looked into her face.

raw: Her eyes were dilated and wild, and she constantly uttered piercing shrieks, and repeated the words, ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ and then counted up to twelve, and said, ‘Hush!’ For an instant, and no more, she would pause to listen, and then the piercing shrieks would begin again, and she would repeat the cry, ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ and would count up to twelve, and say, ‘Hush!’ There was no variation in the order, or the manner.
en: Her eyes were wide and wild, and she kept screaming and repeating the words, ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ She would then count up to twelve and say, ‘Hush!’ For just a second, she would stop to listen, and then the piercing screams would start all over again. She would repeat the cry, ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ count to twelve, and say, ‘Hush!’ She never changed the order or the way she said it.

raw: There was no cessation, but the regular moment’s pause, in the utterance of these sounds.
en: She never stopped, except for that regular, brief moment of listening.

raw: “‘How long,’ I asked, ‘has this lasted?’
en: “‘How long,’ I asked, ‘has this been going on?’

raw: “To distinguish the brothers, I will call them the elder and the younger; by the elder, I mean him who exercised the most authority.
en: “To tell the brothers apart, I will call them the older and the younger. By the older, I mean the one who showed the most authority.

raw: It was the elder who replied, ‘Since about this hour last night.’
en: It was the older brother who replied, ‘Since about this time last night.’

raw: “‘She has a husband, a father, and a brother?’
en: “‘Does she have a husband, a father, and a brother?’

raw: “‘A brother.’
en: “‘A brother.’

raw: “‘I do not address her brother?’
en: “‘Am I speaking to her brother?’

raw: “He answered with great contempt, ‘No.’
en: “He answered with great scorn, ‘No.’

raw: “‘She has some recent association with the number twelve?’
en: “‘Has she recently associated something with the number twelve?’

raw: “The younger brother impatiently rejoined, ‘With twelve o’clock?’
en: “The younger brother added impatiently, ‘With twelve o'clock?’

raw: “‘See, gentlemen,’ said I, still keeping my hands upon her breast, ‘how useless I am, as you have brought me!
en: “‘Look, gentlemen,’ I said, keeping my hands on her chest, ‘I am useless to you since you brought me here like this!

raw: If I had known what I was coming to see, I could have come provided.
en: If I had known what kind of case I was coming to see, I could have brought the right supplies.

raw: As it is, time must be lost.
en: Now we must waste time.

raw: There are no medicines to be obtained in this lonely place.’
en: There are no medicines to be found in this lonely place.’

raw: “The elder brother looked to the younger, who said haughtily, ‘There is a case of medicines here;’ and brought it from a closet, and put it on the table.
en: “The older brother looked at the younger, who said proudly, ‘There is a box of medicines here,’ and brought it out of a closet, placing it on the table.

raw: ***** “I opened some of the bottles, smelt them, and put the stoppers to my lips.
en: “I opened some of the bottles, smelled them, and put the stoppers to my lips.

raw: If I had wanted to use anything save narcotic medicines that were poisons in themselves, I would not have administered any of those.
en: If I had wanted to use anything other than strong sedatives, which are poisons in large doses, I would not have used any of them.

raw: “‘Do you doubt them?’ asked the younger brother.
en: “‘Do you doubt the medicines?’ asked the younger brother.

raw: “‘You see, monsieur, I am going to use them,’ I replied, and said no more.
en: “‘You see, monsieur, I am about to use them,’ I replied, and said nothing more.

raw: “I made the patient swallow, with great difficulty, and after many efforts, the dose that I desired to give.
en: “With great difficulty and after many attempts, I got the patient to swallow the dose I wanted to give her.

raw: As I intended to repeat it after a while, and as it was necessary to watch its influence, I then sat down by the side of the bed.
en: Since I planned to give it to her again later and needed to watch how it affected her, I sat down next to the bed.

raw: There was a timid and suppressed woman in attendance (wife of the man down-stairs), who had retreated into a corner.
en: There was a quiet, timid woman helping, the wife of the servant downstairs, who had shrunk into a corner.

raw: The house was damp and decayed, indifferently furnished--evidently, recently occupied and temporarily used.
en: The house was damp, decaying, and poorly furnished, clearly it had been occupied recently and only for temporary use.

raw: Some thick old hangings had been nailed up before the windows, to deaden the sound of the shrieks.
en: Thick old curtains had been nailed over the windows to muffle the sound of her screams.

raw: They continued to be uttered in their regular succession, with the cry, ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ the counting up to twelve, and ‘Hush!’ The frenzy was so violent, that I had not unfastened the bandages restraining the arms; but, I had looked to them, to see that they were not painful.
en: She kept screaming in the same regular order: the cry of ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!’ the count to twelve, and ‘Hush!’ Her madness was so violent that I did not loosen the bandages holding her arms, though I checked to make sure they were not hurting her.

raw: The only spark of encouragement in the case, was, that my hand upon the sufferer’s breast had this much soothing influence, that for minutes at a time it tranquillised the figure.
en: The only encouraging sign was that my hand on the poor girl's chest had a soothing effect, quietening her body for minutes at a time.

raw: It had no effect upon the cries; no pendulum could be more regular.
en: However, it did not stop her cries; no clock pendulum could have been more regular.

raw: “For the reason that my hand had this effect (I assume), I had sat by the side of the bed for half an hour, with the two brothers looking on, before the elder said:
en: “Probably because my hand had this calming effect, I sat by the bedside for half an hour with the two brothers watching before the older one spoke:

raw: “‘There is another patient.’
en: “‘There is another patient.’

raw: “I was startled, and asked, ‘Is it a pressing case?’
en: “I was startled and asked, ‘Is it an urgent case?’

raw: “‘You had better see,’ he carelessly answered; and took up a light. *****
en: “‘You had better see for yourself,’ he answered carelessly, and picked up a candle.

raw: “The other patient lay in a back room across a second staircase, which was a species of loft over a stable.
en: “The other patient was in a back room across a second staircase, which was a kind of loft over a stable.

raw: There was a low plastered ceiling to a part of it; the rest was open, to the ridge of the tiled roof, and there were beams across.
en: Part of the room had a low, plastered ceiling, while the rest was open to the tiled roof with wooden beams running across.

raw: Hay and straw were stored in that portion of the place, fagots for firing, and a heap of apples in sand.
en: Hay and straw were stored in that part of the loft, along with firewood and a pile of apples stored in sand.

raw: I had to pass through that part, to get at the other.
en: I had to walk through that storage area to reach the patient.

raw: My memory is circumstantial and unshaken.
en: My memory is detailed and firm.

raw: I try it with these details, and I see them all, in this my cell in the Bastille, near the close of the tenth year of my captivity, as I saw them all that night.
en: I test it with these details, and I can see them all here in my Bastille cell, near the end of the tenth year of my imprisonment, just as I saw them that night.

raw: “On some hay on the ground, with a cushion thrown under his head, lay a handsome peasant boy--a boy of not more than seventeen at the most.
en: “On some hay on the ground, with a cushion placed under his head, lay a handsome peasant boy, he could not have been more than seventeen years old.

raw: He lay on his back, with his teeth set, his right hand clenched on his breast, and his glaring eyes looking straight upward.
en: He lay on his back with his teeth clenched, his right hand pressed tightly against his chest, and his staring eyes looking straight up.

raw: I could not see where his wound was, as I kneeled on one knee over him; but, I could see that he was dying of a wound from a sharp point.
en: I could not see where his wound was as I knelt beside him, but I could tell he was dying from a puncture wound.

raw: “‘I am a doctor, my poor fellow,’ said I. ‘Let me examine it.’
en: “‘I am a doctor, my poor boy,’ I said. ‘Let me look at your wound.’

raw: “‘I do not want it examined,’ he answered; ‘let it be.’
en: “‘I don't want it examined,’ he answered. ‘Leave it alone.’

raw: “It was under his hand, and I soothed him to let me move his hand away.
en: “The wound was under his hand, and I calmed him until he let me move his hand away.

raw: The wound was a sword-thrust, received from twenty to twenty-four hours before, but no skill could have saved him if it had been looked to without delay.
en: It was a sword wound received twenty to twenty-four hours earlier, but no medical skill could have saved him even if he had been treated immediately.

raw: He was then dying fast.
en: He was dying fast.

raw: As I turned my eyes to the elder brother, I saw him looking down at this handsome boy whose life was ebbing out, as if he were a wounded bird, or hare, or rabbit; not at all as if he were a fellow-creature.
en: When I looked up at the older brother, I saw him looking down at this handsome, dying boy as if he were just a wounded bird, a hare, or a rabbit, not a fellow human being at all.

raw: “‘How has this been done, monsieur?’ said I.
en: “‘How did this happen, monsieur?’ I asked.

raw: “‘A crazed young common dog!
en: “‘A crazy young peasant dog!

raw: A serf!
en: A serf!

raw: Forced my brother to draw upon him, and has fallen by my brother’s sword--like a gentleman.’
en: He forced my brother to draw his sword against him, and fell by my brother's blade, like a gentleman.’

raw: “There was no touch of pity, sorrow, or kindred humanity, in this answer.
en: “There was no trace of pity, sadness, or human feeling in his answer.

raw: The speaker seemed to acknowledge that it was inconvenient to have that different order of creature dying there, and that it would have been better if he had died in the usual obscure routine of his vermin kind.
en: The speaker spoke as if it were simply inconvenient to have this lower kind of creature dying there, and that it would have been better if he had died in the usual quiet way of his vermin class.

raw: He was quite incapable of any compassionate feeling about the boy, or about his fate.
en: He was completely unable to feel any sympathy for the boy or his fate.

raw: “The boy’s eyes had slowly moved to him as he had spoken, and they now slowly moved to me.
en: “The boy's eyes had moved slowly to the man as he spoke, and now they slowly turned to me.

raw: “‘Doctor, they are very proud, these Nobles; but we common dogs are proud too, sometimes.
en: “‘Doctor, they are very proud, these Nobles; but we common dogs are proud too, sometimes.

raw: They plunder us, outrage us, beat us, kill us; but we have a little pride left, sometimes.
en: They rob us, abuse us, beat us, and kill us, but we still have a little pride left sometimes.

raw: She--have you seen her, Doctor?’
en: She, have you seen her, Doctor?’

raw: “The shrieks and the cries were audible there, though subdued by the distance.
en: “Her screams and cries could be heard there, though they were quieted by the distance.

raw: He referred to them, as if she were lying in our presence.
en: He spoke of her as if she were lying right there with us.

raw: “I said, ‘I have seen her.’
en: “I said, ‘I have seen her.’

raw: “‘She is my sister, Doctor.
en: “‘She is my sister, Doctor.

raw: They have had their shameful rights, these Nobles, in the modesty and virtue of our sisters, many years, but we have had good girls among us.
en: For many years, these Nobles have taken their shameful rights with our sisters' modesty and virtue, but we have had good girls among us.

raw: I know it, and have heard my father say so.
en: I know it, and I've heard my father say so.

raw: She was a good girl.
en: She was a good girl.

raw: She was betrothed to a good young man, too: a tenant of his.
en: She was engaged to a good young man, too, who was a tenant of his.

raw: We were all tenants of his--that man’s who stands there.
en: We were all tenants of his, that man standing there.

raw: The other is his brother, the worst of a bad race.’
en: The other one is his brother, the worst of a bad family.’

raw: “It was with the greatest difficulty that the boy gathered bodily force to speak; but, his spirit spoke with a dreadful emphasis.
en: “It was extremely hard for the boy to find the strength to speak, but his spirit spoke with terrifying power.

raw: “‘We were so robbed by that man who stands there, as all we common dogs are by those superior Beings--taxed by him without mercy, obliged to work for him without pay, obliged to grind our corn at his mill, obliged to feed scores of his tame birds on our wretched crops, and forbidden for our lives to keep a single tame bird of our own, pillaged and plundered to that degree that when we chanced to have a bit of meat, we ate it in fear, with the door barred and the shutters closed, that his people should not see it and take it from us--I say, we were so robbed, and hunted, and were made so poor, that our father told us it was a dreadful thing to bring a child into the world, and that what we should most pray for, was, that our women might be barren and our miserable race die out!’
en: “‘We were robbed so badly by that man standing there, just as all of us common dogs are by those superior Beings, taxed by him without mercy, forced to work for him without pay, forced to grind our grain at his mill, forced to feed dozens of his tame birds on our poor crops, while we were forbidden under pain of death to keep a single tame bird of our own. We were plundered to the point that if we happened to have a piece of meat, we ate it in fear with the door locked and the shutters closed so his servants wouldn't see it and take it from us. I tell you, we were so robbed and hunted, and made so poor, that our father told us it was a terrible thing to bring a child into the world. He said we should pray that our women would be barren and our miserable family line would die out!’

raw: “I had never before seen the sense of being oppressed, bursting forth like a fire.
en: “I had never before seen the pain of oppression burst out like a fire.

raw: I had supposed that it must be latent in the people somewhere; but, I had never seen it break out, until I saw it in the dying boy.
en: I had assumed it must be hidden in the common people somewhere, but I had never seen it break out until I saw it in this dying boy.

raw: “‘Nevertheless, Doctor, my sister married.
en: “‘Even so, Doctor, my sister married.

raw: He was ailing at that time, poor fellow, and she married her lover, that she might tend and comfort him in our cottage--our dog-hut, as that man would call it.
en: Her lover was sick at the time, poor guy, and she married him so she could care for and comfort him in our cottage, our dog-hut, as that nobleman would call it.

raw: She had not been married many weeks, when that man’s brother saw her and admired her, and asked that man to lend her to him--for what are husbands among us!
en: She had only been married a few weeks when that man's brother saw her, took a liking to her, and asked that nobleman to lend her to him, because what are husbands to people like us!

raw: He was willing enough, but my sister was good and virtuous, and hated his brother with a hatred as strong as mine.
en: The nobleman was willing enough, but my sister was good and pure, and she hated the brother as much as I did.

raw: What did the two then, to persuade her husband to use his influence with her, to make her willing?’
en: So what did the two of them do to force her husband to make her give in?’

raw: “The boy’s eyes, which had been fixed on mine, slowly turned to the looker-on, and I saw in the two faces that all he said was true.
en: “The boy's eyes, which had been fixed on mine, turned slowly toward the older brother, and I could see from both of their faces that everything he said was true.

raw: The two opposing kinds of pride confronting one another, I can see, even in this Bastille; the gentleman’s, all negligent indifference; the peasant’s, all trodden-down sentiment, and passionate revenge.
en: Even now in the Bastille, I can still picture those two opposite kinds of pride facing each other: the nobleman's careless indifference, and the peasant's crushed feelings and passionate desire for revenge.

raw: “‘You know, Doctor, that it is among the Rights of these Nobles to harness us common dogs to carts, and drive us.
en: “‘You know, Doctor, that these Nobles have the legal right to harness us common dogs to carts and drive us like horses.

raw: They so harnessed him and drove him.
en: They harnessed him and drove him that way.

raw: You know that it is among their Rights to keep us in their grounds all night, quieting the frogs, in order that their noble sleep may not be disturbed.
en: You know it is their right to keep us in their swamps all night, beating the water to quiet the frogs so their noble sleep won't be disturbed.

raw: They kept him out in the unwholesome mists at night, and ordered him back into his harness in the day.
en: They kept him out in the unhealthy night mists and ordered him back to work during the day.

raw: But he was not persuaded.
en: But he would not give in.

raw: No!
en: No!

raw: Taken out of harness one day at noon, to feed--if he could find food--he sobbed twelve times, once for every stroke of the bell, and died on her bosom.’
en: Taken out of the harness one day at noon to eat, if he could find any food, he sobbed twelve times, once for each strike of the clock, and died in her arms.’

raw: “Nothing human could have held life in the boy but his determination to tell all his wrong.
en: "Nothing human could have kept the boy alive except his determination to tell of his wrongs.

raw: He forced back the gathering shadows of death, as he forced his clenched right hand to remain clenched, and to cover his wound.
en: He fought off the approaching shadows of death, just as he forced his clenched right hand to stay closed over his wound.

raw: “‘Then, with that man’s permission and even with his aid, his brother took her away; in spite of what I know she must have told his brother--and what that is, will not be long unknown to you, Doctor, if it is now--his brother took her away--for his pleasure and diversion, for a little while.
en: “‘Then, with that nobleman's permission and even his help, his brother took her away. In spite of what I know she must have told the brother, and you will find out what that was soon enough, Doctor, if you don't know already, his brother took her away for his own pleasure and amusement for a little while.

raw: I saw her pass me on the road.
en: I saw her pass me on the road.

raw: When I took the tidings home, our father’s heart burst; he never spoke one of the words that filled it.
en: When I brought the news home, our father's heart broke; he died without saying a word of the pain that filled him.

raw: I took my young sister (for I have another) to a place beyond the reach of this man, and where, at least, she will never be _his_ vassal.
en: I took my youngest sister, for I have another one, to a place far away out of this man's reach, where she will never be _his_ servant.

raw: Then, I tracked the brother here, and last night climbed in--a common dog, but sword in hand.--Where is the loft window?
en: Then I followed the brother here, and last night I climbed in, a common dog, but with a sword in my hand. Where is the loft window?

raw: It was somewhere here?’
en: It was around here somewhere.’

raw: “The room was darkening to his sight; the world was narrowing around him.
en: “The room was growing dark to his eyes; the world was closing in on him.

raw: I glanced about me, and saw that the hay and straw were trampled over the floor, as if there had been a struggle.
en: I looked around and saw that the hay and straw were scattered all over the floor, as if there had been a fight.

raw: “‘She heard me, and ran in.
en: “‘She heard me and ran in.

raw: I told her not to come near us till he was dead.
en: I told her not to come near us until he was dead.

raw: He came in and first tossed me some pieces of money; then struck at me with a whip.
en: He came in and first threw some coins at me, then struck at me with a whip.

raw: But I, though a common dog, so struck at him as to make him draw.
en: But even though I am a common dog, I attacked him so hard that I forced him to draw his sword.

raw: Let him break into as many pieces as he will, the sword that he stained with my common blood; he drew to defend himself--thrust at me with all his skill for his life.’
en: Let him break that sword into a thousand pieces, the sword he stained with my common blood, but he had to draw it to defend himself and fight with all his skill for his life.’

raw: “My glance had fallen, but a few moments before, on the fragments of a broken sword, lying among the hay.
en: “Just a few moments earlier, my eyes had fallen on the pieces of a broken sword lying in the hay.

raw: That weapon was a gentleman’s.
en: That weapon belonged to a gentleman.

raw: In another place, lay an old sword that seemed to have been a soldier’s.
en: In another spot lay an old sword that looked like it had belonged to a soldier.

raw: “‘Now, lift me up, Doctor; lift me up.
en: “‘Now lift me up, Doctor; lift me up.

raw: Where is he?’
en: Where is he?’

raw: “‘He is not here,’ I said, supporting the boy, and thinking that he referred to the brother.
en: “‘He is not here,’ I said, holding the boy up, thinking he was talking about the brother.

raw: “‘He!
en: “‘Him!

raw: Proud as these nobles are, he is afraid to see me.
en: As proud as these nobles are, he is afraid to look at me.

raw: Where is the man who was here?
en: Where is the man who was standing here?

raw: Turn my face to him.’
en: Turn my face toward him.’

raw: “I did so, raising the boy’s head against my knee.
en: “I did so, resting the boy's head against my knee.

raw: But, invested for the moment with extraordinary power, he raised himself completely: obliging me to rise too, or I could not have still supported him.
en: But suddenly filled with an unbelievable strength, he pulled himself all the way up, forcing me to stand up too so I could keep supporting him.

raw: “‘Marquis,’ said the boy, turned to him with his eyes opened wide, and his right hand raised, ‘in the days when all these things are to be answered for, I summon you and yours, to the last of your bad race, to answer for them.
en: “‘Marquis,’ the boy said, turning to him with wide eyes and his right hand raised, ‘in the days when all these things must be answered for, I summon you and your family, to the very last of your evil race, to answer for them.

raw: I mark this cross of blood upon you, as a sign that I do it.
en: I mark this cross of blood upon you as a sign of my summons.

raw: In the days when all these things are to be answered for, I summon your brother, the worst of the bad race, to answer for them separately.
en: In the days when all these things must be answered for, I summon your brother, the worst of your evil family, to answer for them separately.

raw: I mark this cross of blood upon him, as a sign that I do it.’
en: I mark this cross of blood upon him as a sign of my summons.’

raw: “Twice, he put his hand to the wound in his breast, and with his forefinger drew a cross in the air.
en: “Twice he touched the wound in his chest and drew a cross in the air with his index finger.

raw: He stood for an instant with the finger yet raised, and as it dropped, he dropped with it, and I laid him down dead.
en: He stood for a moment with his finger still raised, and when it fell, he fell with it. I laid him down, dead.

raw: ***** “When I returned to the bedside of the young woman, I found her raving in precisely the same order of continuity.
en: “When I went back to the young woman's bedside, I found her screaming in the exact same order as before.

raw: I knew that this might last for many hours, and that it would probably end in the silence of the grave.
en: I knew this might go on for many hours, and that it would likely end only in death.

raw: “I repeated the medicines I had given her, and I sat at the side of the bed until the night was far advanced.
en: “I gave her another dose of the medicine and sat by the bed until late in the night.

raw: She never abated the piercing quality of her shrieks, never stumbled in the distinctness or the order of her words.
en: She never stopped her piercing screams, and never made a mistake in the clear order of her words.

raw: They were always ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!
en: They were always: ‘My husband, my father, and my brother!

raw: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve.
en: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve.

raw: Hush!’
en: Hush!’

raw: “This lasted twenty-six hours from the time when I first saw her.
en: “This went on for twenty-six hours from the time I first saw her.

raw: I had come and gone twice, and was again sitting by her, when she began to falter.
en: I had left and returned twice, and was sitting by her again when her strength began to fail.

raw: I did what little could be done to assist that opportunity, and by-and-bye she sank into a lethargy, and lay like the dead. “It was as if the wind and rain had lulled at last, after a long and fearful storm.
en: I did what little I could to help her rest, and soon she fell into a deep sleep and lay as still as a corpse. It was as if the wind and rain had finally stopped after a long, terrifying storm.

raw: I released her arms, and called the woman to assist me to compose her figure and the dress she had torn.
en: I untied her arms and called the servant's wife to help me straighten her body and the clothes she had torn.

raw: It was then that I knew her condition to be that of one in whom the first expectations of being a mother have arisen; and it was then that I lost the little hope I had had of her.
en: It was then I realized she was pregnant, and at that moment I lost the little hope I had left for her.

raw: “‘Is she dead?’ asked the Marquis, whom I will still describe as the elder brother, coming booted into the room from his horse.
en: “‘Is she dead?’ asked the Marquis, the older brother, walking into the room still wearing his riding boots.

raw: “‘Not dead,’ said I; ‘but like to die.’
en: “‘Not dead,’ I said, ‘but close to it.’

raw: “‘What strength there is in these common bodies!’ he said, looking down at her with some curiosity.
en: “‘What strength there is in these peasant bodies!’ he said, looking down at her with curiosity.

raw: “‘There is prodigious strength,’ I answered him, ‘in sorrow and despair.’
en: “‘There is enormous strength,’ I answered him, ‘in grief and despair.’

raw: “He first laughed at my words, and then frowned at them.
en: “He laughed at my words at first, then frowned.

raw: He moved a chair with his foot near to mine, ordered the woman away, and said in a subdued voice,
en: He kicked a chair over near mine, ordered the woman to leave, and said in a quiet voice:

raw: “‘Doctor, finding my brother in this difficulty with these hinds, I recommended that your aid should be invited.
en: “‘Doctor, when I found my brother in this trouble with these peasants, I suggested we call for your help.

raw: Your reputation is high, and, as a young man with your fortune to make, you are probably mindful of your interest.
en: Your reputation is high, and as a young man trying to make a career, you probably care about your own success.

raw: The things that you see here, are things to be seen, and not spoken of.’
en: The things you see here are meant to be seen, but never spoken of.’

raw: “I listened to the patient’s breathing, and avoided answering.
en: “I listened to the patient's breathing and avoided answering him.

raw: “‘Do you honour me with your attention, Doctor?’
en: “‘Are you listening to me, Doctor?’

raw: “‘Monsieur,’ said I, ‘in my profession, the communications of patients are always received in confidence.’ I was guarded in my answer, for I was troubled in my mind with what I had heard and seen.
en: “‘Monsieur,’ I said, ‘in my profession, whatever a patient tells a doctor is always kept strictly confidential.’ I was careful with my reply because I was deeply troubled by what I had seen and heard.

raw: “Her breathing was so difficult to trace, that I carefully tried the pulse and the heart.
en: “Her breathing was so faint that I carefully checked her pulse and heartbeat.

raw: There was life, and no more.
en: She was barely alive.

raw: Looking round as I resumed my seat, I found both the brothers intent upon me.
en: Looking up as I sat back down, I saw both brothers watching me closely.

raw: ***** “I write with so much difficulty, the cold is so severe, I am so fearful of being detected and consigned to an underground cell and total darkness, that I must abridge this narrative.
en: “I write with so much difficulty, the cold is so bitter, and I am so afraid of being caught and thrown into a dark dungeon that I must shorten this story.

raw: There is no confusion or failure in my memory; it can recall, and could detail, every word that was ever spoken between me and those brothers.
en: There is no confusion or memory loss; I can remember and detail every single word spoken between me and those brothers.

raw: “She lingered for a week.
en: “She hung onto life for a week.

raw: Towards the last, I could understand some few syllables that she said to me, by placing my ear close to her lips.
en: Near the end, I could make out a few words she whispered by putting my ear close to her lips.

raw: She asked me where she was, and I told her; who I was, and I told her.
en: She asked me where she was and who I was, and I told her.

raw: It was in vain that I asked her for her family name.
en: I tried in vain to ask for her family name.

raw: She faintly shook her head upon the pillow, and kept her secret, as the boy had done.
en: She just shook her head weakly on the pillow, keeping her secret just as her brother had done.

raw: “I had no opportunity of asking her any question, until I had told the brothers she was sinking fast, and could not live another day.
en: "I had no chance to ask her any questions until I told the brothers she was dying and could not last another day.

raw: Until then, though no one was ever presented to her consciousness save the woman and myself, one or other of them had always jealously sat behind the curtain at the head of the bed when I was there.
en: Until then, even though she only saw the servant's wife and me, one of the brothers had always sat watchfully behind the curtain at the head of the bed whenever I was there.

raw: But when it came to that, they seemed careless what communication I might hold with her; as if--the thought passed through my mind--I were dying too.
en: But when she was near death, they didn't seem to care what I said to her, as if, a sudden thought struck me, they planned for me to die too.

raw: “I always observed that their pride bitterly resented the younger brother’s (as I call him) having crossed swords with a peasant, and that peasant a boy.
en: “I noticed that their pride was deeply hurt by the fact that the younger brother had fought a peasant boy.

raw: The only consideration that appeared to affect the mind of either of them was the consideration that this was highly degrading to the family, and was ridiculous.
en: The only thing that seemed to bother either of them was that this fight was degrading to their family name and made them look ridiculous.

raw: As often as I caught the younger brother’s eyes, their expression reminded me that he disliked me deeply, for knowing what I knew from the boy.
en: Whenever I met the younger brother's eyes, I could see that he hated me for knowing what the dying boy had told me.

raw: He was smoother and more polite to me than the elder; but I saw this.
en: He was more polite and pleasant to me than the older brother, but I could see right through him.

raw: I also saw that I was an incumbrance in the mind of the elder, too.
en: I also realized that the older brother saw me as an annoying problem to be dealt with.

raw: “My patient died, two hours before midnight--at a time, by my watch, answering almost to the minute when I had first seen her.
en: “My patient died two hours before midnight, almost to the exact minute I had first seen her a week earlier.

raw: I was alone with her, when her forlorn young head drooped gently on one side, and all her earthly wrongs and sorrows ended.
en: I was alone with her when her poor, young head fell gently to the side, and all her earthly pain and sorrows ended.

raw: “The brothers were waiting in a room down-stairs, impatient to ride away.
en: “The brothers were waiting in a room downstairs, eager to ride away.

raw: I had heard them, alone at the bedside, striking their boots with their riding-whips, and loitering up and down.
en: While I sat alone by the bedside, I had heard them pacing up and down, tapping their boots with their riding whips.

raw: “‘At last she is dead?’ said the elder, when I went in.
en: “‘Is she finally dead?’ the older one asked when I went downstairs.

raw: “‘She is dead,’ said I.
en: “‘She is dead,’ I said.

raw: “‘I congratulate you, my brother,’ were his words as he turned round.
en: “‘Congratulations, brother,’ he said, turning to his twin.

raw: “He had before offered me money, which I had postponed taking.
en: “He had offered me money earlier, which I had put off taking.

raw: He now gave me a rouleau of gold.
en: Now he handed me a roll of gold coins.

raw: I took it from his hand, but laid it on the table.
en: I took it from his hand but set it down on the table.

raw: I had considered the question, and had resolved to accept nothing.
en: I had thought it over and decided not to accept anything from them.

raw: “‘Pray excuse me,’ said I. ‘Under the circumstances, no.’
en: “‘Please excuse me,’ I said. ‘Under these circumstances, I cannot take it.’

raw: “They exchanged looks, but bent their heads to me as I bent mine to them, and we parted without another word on either side. *****
en: “They looked at each other, but bowed their heads to me as I bowed to them, and we parted without saying another word.

raw: “I am weary, weary, weary--worn down by misery.
en: “I am so tired, tired, tired, worn down by misery.

raw: I cannot read what I have written with this gaunt hand.
en: I can barely read what my thin hand has written.

raw: “Early in the morning, the rouleau of gold was left at my door in a little box, with my name on the outside.
en: “Early the next morning, the roll of gold was left at my door in a small box with my name written on it.

raw: From the first, I had anxiously considered what I ought to do.
en: From the beginning, I had worried about what I should do.

raw: I decided, that day, to write privately to the Minister, stating the nature of the two cases to which I had been summoned, and the place to which I had gone: in effect, stating all the circumstances.
en: That day, I decided to write a private letter to the government Minister, explaining the two patients I had been called to see, the location of the house, and all the details.

raw: I knew what Court influence was, and what the immunities of the Nobles were, and I expected that the matter would never be heard of; but, I wished to relieve my own mind.
en: I knew how much influence the Nobles had at Court and how they were above the law, so I expected nothing would be done about it; however, I wanted to clear my own conscience.

raw: I had kept the matter a profound secret, even from my wife; and this, too, I resolved to state in my letter.
en: I had kept the secret completely from my wife, and I decided to mention that in the letter too.

raw: I had no apprehension whatever of my real danger; but I was conscious that there might be danger for others, if others were compromised by possessing the knowledge that I possessed.
en: I had no fear for my own safety, but I knew there could be danger for others if they were dragged into this by knowing what I knew.

raw: “I was much engaged that day, and could not complete my letter that night.
en: “I was very busy that day and couldn't finish the letter that night.

raw: I rose long before my usual time next morning to finish it.
en: I woke up long before my usual time the next morning to complete it.

raw: It was the last day of the year.
en: It was the last day of the year.

raw: The letter was lying before me just completed, when I was told that a lady waited, who wished to see me. *****
en: The letter was lying finished on the desk in front of me when I was told that a lady was waiting to see me.

raw: “I am growing more and more unequal to the task I have set myself.
en: “I am becoming less and less able to finish this task.

raw: It is so cold, so dark, my senses are so benumbed, and the gloom upon me is so dreadful.
en: It is so cold and dark, my senses are so numb, and the sadness around me is so terrible.

raw: “The lady was young, engaging, and handsome, but not marked for long life.
en: “The lady was young, charming, and beautiful, but she looked pale and weak.

raw: She was in great agitation.
en: She was extremely upset.

raw: She presented herself to me as the wife of the Marquis St.
en: She introduced herself as the wife of the Marquis St.

raw: Evrémonde.
en: Evrémonde.

raw: I connected the title by which the boy had addressed the elder brother, with the initial letter embroidered on the scarf, and had no difficulty in arriving at the conclusion that I had seen that nobleman very lately.
en: I connected the title the dying boy had used for the older brother with the letter embroidered on the scarf, and immediately realized I had met her husband very recently.

raw: “My memory is still accurate, but I cannot write the words of our conversation.
en: “My memory is still clear, but I cannot write down all the words of our conversation.

raw: I suspect that I am watched more closely than I was, and I know not at what times I may be watched.
en: I suspect I am being watched more closely now, and I do not know when they are spying on me.

raw: She had in part suspected, and in part discovered, the main facts of the cruel story, of her husband’s share in it, and my being resorted to.
en: She had guessed some of the facts and discovered the rest of the cruel story, her husband's part in it, and how they had called for my help.

raw: She did not know that the girl was dead.
en: She did not know the young woman had died.

raw: Her hope had been, she said in great distress, to show her, in secret, a woman’s sympathy.
en: She told me in great distress that she had hoped to show the poor girl a woman's sympathy in secret.

raw: Her hope had been to avert the wrath of Heaven from a House that had long been hateful to the suffering many.
en: She had hoped to turn away God's anger from a noble family that had long been hated by the suffering people.

raw: “She had reasons for believing that there was a young sister living, and her greatest desire was, to help that sister.
en: “She had reasons to believe there was a younger sister still alive, and her greatest wish was to help her.

raw: I could tell her nothing but that there was such a sister; beyond that, I knew nothing.
en: I could only tell her that the sister did exist; beyond that, I knew nothing.

raw: Her inducement to come to me, relying on my confidence, had been the hope that I could tell her the name and place of abode.
en: She had come to me, trusting my confidentiality, hoping I could tell her the girl's name and where she lived.

raw: Whereas, to this wretched hour I am ignorant of both.
en: But to this miserable hour, I still know neither.

raw: ***** “These scraps of paper fail me.
en: “I am running out of paper.

raw: One was taken from me, with a warning, yesterday.
en: One piece was taken from me yesterday, along with a warning.

raw: I must finish my record to-day.
en: I must finish my record today.

raw: “She was a good, compassionate lady, and not happy in her marriage.
en: “She was a good, kind lady, and she was not happy in her marriage.

raw: How could she be!
en: How could she be!

raw: The brother distrusted and disliked her, and his influence was all opposed to her; she stood in dread of him, and in dread of her husband too.
en: The brother-in-law distrusted and disliked her, and his influence was completely against her; she was terrified of him, and of her husband too.

raw: When I handed her down to the door, there was a child, a pretty boy from two to three years old, in her carriage.
en: When I walked her down to the carriage, I saw a child inside, a pretty little boy about two or three years old.

raw: “‘For his sake, Doctor,’ she said, pointing to him in tears, ‘I would do all I can to make what poor amends I can.
en: “‘For his sake, Doctor,’ she said, pointing to the boy through her tears, ‘I want to do everything I can to make up for this.

raw: He will never prosper in his inheritance otherwise.
en: Otherwise, he will never find happiness in his inheritance.

raw: I have a presentiment that if no other innocent atonement is made for this, it will one day be required of him.
en: I have a feeling that if no other innocent person pays for this crime, it will one day be demanded of him.

raw: What I have left to call my own--it is little beyond the worth of a few jewels--I will make it the first charge of his life to bestow, with the compassion and lamenting of his dead mother, on this injured family, if the sister can be discovered.’
en: The little I have of my own, which is hardly more than a few jewels, I will make it his first duty in life to give to this injured family, along with the love and sorrow of his dead mother, if the sister can be found.’

raw: “She kissed the boy, and said, caressing him, ‘It is for thine own dear sake.
en: “She kissed the boy and said as she held him close, ‘It is for your own dear sake.

raw: Thou wilt be faithful, little Charles?’ The child answered her bravely, ‘Yes!’ I kissed her hand, and she took him in her arms, and went away caressing him.
en: You will be faithful to this promise, little Charles?’ The child answered her bravely, ‘Yes!’ I kissed her hand, and she took him in her arms and drove away.

raw: I never saw her more.
en: I never saw her again.

raw: “As she had mentioned her husband’s name in the faith that I knew it, I added no mention of it to my letter.
en: “Since she had mentioned her husband's name, assuming I already knew it, I did not add it to my letter.

raw: I sealed my letter, and, not trusting it out of my own hands, delivered it myself that day.
en: I sealed the envelope, and not trusting anyone else, I delivered it myself that day.

raw: “That night, the last night of the year, towards nine o’clock, a man in a black dress rang at my gate, demanded to see me, and softly followed my servant, Ernest Defarge, a youth, up-stairs.
en: “That night, the last night of the year, around nine o'clock, a man dressed in black rang my doorbell, asked to see me, and quietly followed my young servant, Ernest Defarge, upstairs.

raw: When my servant came into the room where I sat with my wife--O my wife, beloved of my heart! My fair young English wife!--we saw the man, who was supposed to be at the gate, standing silent behind him.
en: When my servant entered the room where I sat with my wife, oh, my beloved wife, the joy of my heart, my beautiful young English wife!, we saw the man standing silently behind him.

raw: “An urgent case in the Rue St. Honore, he said.
en: “He said there was an urgent case on Rue Saint-Honoré.

raw: It would not detain me, he had a coach in waiting.
en: He promised it wouldn't take long and said a carriage was waiting.

raw: “It brought me here, it brought me to my grave.
en: “It brought me here; it brought me to my grave.

raw: When I was clear of the house, a black muffler was drawn tightly over my mouth from behind, and my arms were pinioned.
en: As soon as I stepped out of the house, a black scarf was pulled tightly over my mouth from behind, and my arms were tied.

raw: The two brothers crossed the road from a dark corner, and identified me with a single gesture.
en: The two brothers walked across the road from a dark corner and pointed me out with a simple gesture.

raw: The Marquis took from his pocket the letter I had written, showed it me, burnt it in the light of a lantern that was held, and extinguished the ashes with his foot.
en: The Marquis took the letter I had written from his pocket, showed it to me, burned it in the light of a lantern, and stamped out the ashes with his foot.

raw: Not a word was spoken.
en: Not a single word was spoken.

raw: I was brought here, I was brought to my living grave.
en: I was brought here, to my living grave.

raw: “If it had pleased _God_ to put it in the hard heart of either of the brothers, in all these frightful years, to grant me any tidings of my dearest wife--so much as to let me know by a word whether alive or dead--I might have thought that He had not quite abandoned them.
en: “If it had pleased _God_ to put it in the hard hearts of either of the brothers during all these terrible years to give me any news of my dearest wife, even just a single word to tell me if she was alive or dead, I might have believed that He had not completely abandoned them.

raw: But, now I believe that the mark of the red cross is fatal to them, and that they have no part in His mercies.
en: But now I believe that the mark of the red cross has doomed them, and that they have no share in His mercy.

raw: And them and their descendants, to the last of their race, I, Alexandre Manette, unhappy prisoner, do this last night of the year 1767, in my unbearable agony, denounce to the times when all these things shall be answered for.
en: So, on this last night of the year 1767, in my unbearable agony, I, Alexandre Manette, an unhappy prisoner, denounce them and their descendants to the very last of their family line, to the time when all these crimes must be answered for.

raw: I denounce them to Heaven and to earth.”
en: I denounce them to Heaven and to earth.”

raw: A terrible sound arose when the reading of this document was done.
en: A terrifying noise arose when the reading of this document finished.

raw: A sound of craving and eagerness that had nothing articulate in it but blood.
en: It was a sound of hungry eagerness, with no clear words except a cry for blood.

raw: The narrative called up the most revengeful passions of the time, and there was not a head in the nation but must have dropped before it.
en: The story stirred up the most vengeful feelings of the time, and there was not a noble head in the country that would not have fallen after hearing it.

raw: Little need, in presence of that tribunal and that auditory, to show how the Defarges had not made the paper public, with the other captured Bastille memorials borne in procession, and had kept it, biding their time.
en: There was no need, in front of that court and audience, to explain why the Defarges had not made the paper public with the other captured Bastille records during the parades. They had kept it hidden, waiting for the perfect time.

raw: Little need to show that this detested family name had long been anathematised by Saint Antoine, and was wrought into the fatal register.
en: There was no need to show that this hated family name had long been cursed by the people of Saint Antoine, and was already written in the secret registry.

raw: The man never trod ground whose virtues and services would have sustained him in that place that day, against such denunciation.
en: No man had ever lived whose good deeds and service could have saved him in that courtroom today against such an accusation.

raw: And all the worse for the doomed man, that the denouncer was a well-known citizen, his own attached friend, the father of his wife.
en: And it was all the worse for the doomed man that his accuser was a respected citizen, his own close friend, and his wife's father.

raw: One of the frenzied aspirations of the populace was, for imitations of the questionable public virtues of antiquity, and for sacrifices and self-immolations on the people’s altar.
en: The crowd's crazy desire was to imitate the harsh public virtues of ancient times, offering up human sacrifices on the altar of the people.

raw: Therefore when the President said (else had his own head quivered on his shoulders), that the good physician of the Republic would deserve better still of the Republic by rooting out an obnoxious family of Aristocrats, and would doubtless feel a sacred glow and joy in making his daughter a widow and her child an orphan, there was wild excitement, patriotic fervour, not a touch of human sympathy.
en: Therefore, when the President declared, knowing his own head would roll if he didn't, that the good doctor of the Republic would serve the country even better by wiping out a hated family of aristocrats, and would surely feel a holy joy in making his own daughter a widow and her child an orphan, there was wild excitement and patriotic passion, but not a single drop of human sympathy.

raw: “Much influence around him, has that Doctor?” murmured Madame Defarge, smiling to The Vengeance. “Save him now, my Doctor, save him!”
en: “Does that Doctor have a lot of influence now?” whispered Madame Defarge, smiling at The Vengeance. “Save him now, my Doctor, save him!”

raw: At every juryman’s vote, there was a roar.
en: With every juror's vote, a roar went up.

raw: Another and another.
en: Another and another.

raw: Roar and roar.
en: Roar after roar.

raw: Unanimously voted.
en: The vote was unanimous.

raw: At heart and by descent an Aristocrat, an enemy of the Republic, a notorious oppressor of the People.
en: By birth and by nature an aristocrat, an enemy of the Republic, and a well-known oppressor of the people.

raw: Back to the Conciergerie, and Death within four-and-twenty hours!
en: Back to the Conciergerie prison, and death within twenty-four hours!
